summary_paragraph: A female patient with end-stage renal disease, antiphospholipid syndrome, and a history of failed kidney transplant was admitted for worsening dyspnea and fatigue due to acute diastolic heart failure from volume overload. She was 5 kg above her dry weight, with bilateral pleural effusions and pulmonary edema confirmed on CT, but no pulmonary embolism. She underwent aggressive ultrafiltration via dialysis, leading to clinical improvement. She also had a non-functional left AV fistula with central occlusion, which was ligated successfully. Her warfarin was held perioperatively and resumed at discharge with a therapeutic INR of 1.7. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to monitor weight, continue dialysis, and follow up with surgery and her primary team.
problems: Other complications due to renal dialysis device, implant, and graft
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
